subStrands.name: Nature, Terms, Sources, Approaches and Structure

objectives.description: Introduction to the Study of WATR: characteristics (belief in the Supreme Being, divinities, ancestors, mystical powers); purpose/reasons for the study of WATR.
Terms used to describe WATR: fetishism and paganism, animism and ancestral worship, polytheism and monotheism, totemism, primitive.
Sources of WATR: non-oral sources (traditional arts/crafts); oral sources (names and attributes of God, theophorous names, proverbs/wise sayings, songs/dirges, myths/legends and drum language).
Approaches to the study of WATR: thematic, comparative, historical and enumerative approaches.
Structure of WATR: God in West African belief; the ancestors; the divinities; charms and amulets.
Worship in WATR: introduction; main features (prayer/libation, sacrifice, spirit possession).

subStrands.name: Religious Personalities, Festivals, Medicine, Time, Wealth, Man, Enemies, Ethics and Rites

objectives.description: Religious Personalities: concept/types; processes for selecting religious personalities; functions of religious leaders.
Festivals: types; significance.
Religion and Medicine: introduction; herbal medicine; traditional and orthodox healing.
Concept of Time, Work and Wealth: definition of time; concept of the future; importance of time; meaning and attitude towards wealth; ways of acquiring wealth; consequences of acquiring wealth.
Concept of Man and Destiny; concept of man; concept of destiny.
Enemies of Life: witchcraft and magic (meaning, acquisition, role); malevolent spirits.
Religion and Ethics: main features of ethics; sources of ethics in WATR; moral values/virtues; taboos and sin; covenant in WATR.
Rites of Passage: stages (birth, naming, puberty, marriage and death); importance of rites of passage.

subStrands.name: Politics, Tourism, Stress, Conflict, Reproductive Health, Modernity and New Religious Movements

objectives.description: Traditional Political Institutions: chieftaincy (structure, selection process, importance); Asafo companies (introduction, importance).
Religion and Tourism: religion and tourism; uses of free/leisure time; sacred personalities, places and objects and tourism.
Religion and Stress Management: meaning and types of stress situations; causes and effects; management of stress situations.
The Role of WATR in Conflict Resolution and Management: meaning/concept of conflict; causes, effects; conflict resolution and management in West African society.
Religion and Reproductive Health: WATR and reproductive health features (hygiene, sexuality, promiscuity/abortion); circumcision rites and reproductive health.

WATR and Modernity: impact of foreign religions (Christianity and Islam) on WATR; impact of WATR on Christianity and Islam; impact of science and technology on WATR; WATR and conservation of the environment; impact of urbanisation on WATR.
New Religious Movements (NRM): Godianism (Nigeria); the future of West African Traditional Religion.
